ontology.name: nutrition_ontology_sdk
ontology.description: Manifest for the nutrition ontology as code: object types, interfaces, predicates, entity kinds, spine stages, actions and response types in one file a generator can read. Exploratory — nothing in ontology-sdk/ is normative, and where this disagrees with FDP-1, FDP-1 wins (README.md).

sources.predicates: nutri-collective/evidence-platform/src/mechanism_schema.py — Relation and COMPAT, the one candidate vocabulary with an executed domain/range matrix; copied by hand, re-derived by check_manifest.py when that checkout sits beside this repo
sources.spine_stages: nutri-collective/scripts/migrate_spine_naming.py — the six declared stages (GROUNDED-OBJECT-MODEL.md §2, blockers 1 and 2)
sources.object_types: GROUNDED-OBJECT-MODEL.md §3 and §3a — properties are the fields each register actually carries, not a wish list
sources.interfaces: fdp-1/validator/validate_fdp.py VALUE_FIELDS and SOURCE_TO_GRADE; ontology-sdk/declared.py Declared

notes.spine_stages: An object type's spine_stage is one of the six declared stages or null. null means the type is not on the spine (a catalogue, a vocabulary layer, a product record) and the type's note says why. Principle is a chain, so it carries spine_span instead.
notes.entity_kinds: What predicates are typed over. object_type is the manifest type that realises the kind, or null — a predicate may be typed over a kind no object type yet realises (blockers 3 and 4).
notes.predicates: A hand copy of mechanism_schema.COMPAT, and the settled base (blocker 4, landed 2026-09-03). Every other relation vocabulary this project carries — the law model, the graph, the claim-language lexicon, nutrient-edge.v2, the id-crosswalk kinds, the taxonomy joins — is mapped onto these eleven, verb by verb, in relation-crosswalk.v1.json, which also lists what the base cannot carry (modality, bounds, symmetric interaction, binding, saturation, membership). Extending the base is a decision-ledger row, never an edit in place.
notes.interfaces: Citable is what FDP-1 §2 enforces as a unit; Declared spells method as method_ref, an alias recorded here rather than a second field (blocker 5). Gradeable is implemented by Declared, the SDK wrapper — an FDP-1 Value does not store a grade, it derives one from source.
notes.actions: Declared, not implemented. They name the kinetic verbs DESIGN.md wants; none has code behind it, and a tool must never offer them as callable.

spine:anatomy.note: off-ladder peer: compartments, enzymes, transporters, hormones

Validatable.description: Can assert its conformance against a schema or law.

Citable.description: Carries provenance: where the number came from (source_ref) and how it was obtained (method). FDP-1 §2 enforces source, source_ref, method and retrieved as a unit; source_ref and method are the two that make a value citable.

Falsifiable.description: A dated claim that names what would show it wrong and when it resolves. Scored by reading a register on that date, never by recollection; the score is kept whichever way it went.

Gradeable.description: Carries a provenance grade (A|B|C|D|—) and folds by weakest link: a derived value's grade is the grade of its lowest-graded input (FDP-1 §3.1).

MEDIATES.description: sits on the causal path to a disease

ACTIVATES.description: activates a gene, enzyme or process

INHIBITS.description: inhibits a gene, enzyme or process

OntologyTerm.note: the spine catalogue itself (bfo_stack_ontology.json terms[]); each term carries its own spine_stage

Concept.note: controlled vocabulary — the layer beneath the spine

Principle.note: a mechanism chain, not a stage — it spans three

Claim.note: product record; verdict here is the prose sentence and grade the machine grade — two fields, never one

Value.note: an FDP-1 value declaration; all seven fields are enforced as a unit. Its grade is derived from source by SOURCE_TO_GRADE, not stored, so Gradeable is implemented by the Declared wrapper, not by the record

Law.note: two registers, one id space, different field vocabularies

CrosswalkNode.note: spine:compound holds for the cdno, fdc and infoods namespaces only; the other six namespaces are identity rows off the spine

Standard.note: governance object: a schema, ontology or checklist a study can be structured with; four rows are this project's own proposals, flagged by origin

Organization.note: governance object: an adopter, observed only through the tracker rows that name it — the tracker has no organization table and the manifest does not invent one

AdoptionEvent.note: governance object: one dated stage change on one tracker row; the tracker's rule is that every change is appended when it happens

TrackedSubject.note: governance object: a thing the standardization ledger watches — an adoption row, an organization, a layer score, a trend series, a disclosure floor — by a ref that must resolve to a register row on disk

CapturedEvent.note: governance object: something this project captured about standardization or adoption, dated twice (when it happened, when it was written down), evidenced, and tied to the register field it moved; append-only

Prediction.note: governance object: a pre-registered claim about what a register will record — never a person, a prize or a judgment score; drafts are unsigned, open rows are signed or derived from a field the author owns, resolved rows point at an artifact

Decision.note: governance object: one knob moved by hand in a tuned loop, with what was held fixed, what was observed, what was predicted, what was measured and the verdict; the memory of a closed control loop run by hand

declare_value.description: Appends a validated declaration of a Value.

record_layer_pass.description: Records the passage of an object through an ontology layer check.

Declared.description: The SDK primitive (ontology-sdk/declared.py): a state that is a T, OPEN or NONE — null is not a state — plus grade, method_ref and source_ref.

ActionResponse.description: A wrapper containing either the successful data or a structured refusal.

Refusal.description: Structured reason for an action failing its validation gates.
